content: The text provided is a list of references from various studies, reports, and articles related to male circumcision, particularly in the context of HIV prevention. These references include details about the authors, study designs, outcomes, and publication sources. 1. RT, Manda R, Ntsuape CO, et al. conducted a study in Botswana to explore participant experiences and perceptions of odor and pain associated with the removal of the PrePex device during a voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) pilot study. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016. 2. Mutabazi V, Bitega JP, Ngeruka LM, Hategekimana T, Kaplan SA, and Karema C, among others, investigated the feasibility of task-shifting non-surgical adult male circumcision using the PrePex device from physicians to nurses. This study was published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2014. 3. Mutabazi V, Bitega JP, Ngeruka LM, Karema C, and Binagwaho A assessed odor levels associated with the use of the PrePex device for HIV prevention. This prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-assessor trial aimed to improve the uptake of male circumcision and was published in PLoS One in 2015. 4. Mutabazi V, Kaplan SA, Rwamasirabo E, Bitega JP, Ngeruka ML, and Savio D compared the safety and efficacy of a non-surgical circumcision device to a surgical technique in resource-limited settings. This prospective, randomized, non-masked trial was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012. 5. Mutabazi V, Kaplan SA, Rwamasirabo E, Bitega JP, Ngeruka ML, and Savio D conducted a one-arm, open-label, prospective cohort field study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of the PrePex device for scaling up non-surgical circumcision performed by nurses in resource-limited settings for HIV prevention. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2013. 6. Tshimanga M, Makunike-Chikwinya B, Mangwiro T, Gundidza PT, Chatikobo P, and Murenje V, among others, evaluated the safety and efficacy of the PrePex device in HIV-positive men in Zimbabwe. This single-arm study was published in PLoS One in 2017. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) convened an informal consultation in Geneva, Switzerland, in March 2015, to discuss tetanus and voluntary medical male circumcision. The report is accessible online and was last accessed in September 2019. 8. WHO's Technical Advisory Group on Innovations in Male Circumcision reviewed the risk of tetanus associated with different circumcision methods and risk mitigation strategies. The report, based on a consultative review held in August 2016, is available online and was last accessed in July 2019. 9. Agot K, Ambia J, Bosire R, Muhuaya D, Juma J, and Bitok A, among others, examined the safety and acceptability of PrePex circumcision among adolescents in Kisumu, Kenya. The findings are available online and were last accessed in June 2020. 10. Agot K, Bosire R, Ambia J, Muhuaya D, Juma J, and Onyango M, among others, studied the safety and acceptability of Day 0 foreskin removal using the PrePex device among men in Kenya. The findings were presented in a report accessed in September 2019. 11. Linyama D conducted a field safety and acceptability study of the PrePex male circumcision device, focusing on foreskin removal shortly after device placement. The study was presented at the 9th IAS Conference on HIV Science in Paris, France, in 2017. 12. Otieno F, Obat E, Ochomo B, and Kibet N conducted a prospective, randomized, open-label trial comparing the PrePex Day 7 foreskin removal procedure to the Day 0 procedure in resource-limited settings. The study report was submitted confidentially to WHO in 2017. 13. WHO's Technical Advisory Group on Innovations in Male Circumcision held teleconferences in October 2018 and June 2019 to discuss advancements in male circumcision. The report is available online and was last accessed in June 2020. 14. Fram F, Church F, Sundaram M, Sgaier SK, Ridzon R, and Eletskaya M, among others, utilized demand-based volumetric forecasting to identify the potential and roles of devices in scaling up medical male circumcision in Zambia and Zimbabwe. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016. 15. Milovanovic M, Taruberekera N, Martinson N, and Lebina L explored perceptions of the PrePex device among men who either accepted or refused PrePex circumcision, as well as their accompanying individuals. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016. 16. Tshimanga M, Mangwiro T, Mugurungi O, Xaba S, Murwira M, and Kasprzyk D, among others, conducted a Phase II randomized controlled trial comparing the safety, procedure time, and cost of the PrePex device to forceps-guided surgical circumcision in Zimbabwe. The study was published in PLoS One in 2016. 17. Galukande M, Nakaggwa F, Busisa E, Sekavuga Bbaale D, Nagaddya T, and Coutinho A evaluated long-term outcomes of PrePex male circumcision in an urban population in Uganda. This cohort study was published in BMC Research Notes in 2017. 18. Odoyo-June E, Feldblum PJ, Fischer S, Bailey RC, Obiero W, and Hart C, among others, reported unexpected complications following adult medical male circumcision using the PrePex device. The findings were published in Urologia Internationalis in 2016. 19. Kasprzyk D, Montano DE, Hamilton DT, Down KL, Marrett KD, and Tshimanga M, among others, examined psychosocial outcomes from a Phase I trial of a non-surgical circumcision device for adult men in Zimbabwe. The study was published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2016. 20. Musau P, Demirelli M, Muraguri N, Ndwiga F, Wainaina D, and Ali NA assessed the safety profile and acceptability of a disposable male circumcision device among Kenyan men undergoing voluntary medical male circumcision. The study was published in the Journal of Urology in 2011. This format provides a clear and professional summary of each reference, maintaining the integrity of the original content while making it more accessible to readers.
